# Glossary

Terms in this glossary name recurring design distinctions rather than new S7
APIs. Each definition links to its principal treatment in the book.

Aggregate root

: The object boundary that sees a complete consistency unit and can enforce
  relationships among its contained values. See
  [the checking ladder](04-parse-dont-validate.qmd#one-authoritative-definition-several-uses).

Canonical equality

: Equality after applying documented normalization rules, without requiring
  exact R representation identity. See
  [identity and equality](02-values-and-state.qmd#identity-equality-and-testing).

Contextual preparation

: A named operation that combines an intrinsically valid value with external
  data, metadata, resources, or authority and returns a value recording what
  was resolved. See
  [contextual preparation](04-parse-dont-validate.qmd#contextual-preparation).

Domain equality

: Equality defined by meaning in the problem domain rather than exact storage
  representation. See
  [round-trip equivalence](06-documents-schemas-dsls.qmd#round-trips-require-named-equivalence).

Invariant

: A condition that must remain true for a value or consistency boundary
  throughout its supported lifecycle. See
  [retained knowledge](04-parse-dont-validate.qmd#keep-the-result-of-checking).

Operation contract

: The meaning, accepted concepts, result, failure policy, and laws shared by
  every implementation of an operation. See
  [defining operations](05-composition-and-dispatch.qmd#define-the-operation-before-its-methods).

Property contract

: The class, shape, cardinality, presence policy, default behavior, and
  intrinsic constraints attached to one property position. See
  [the property inventory](03-types-and-meaning.qmd#a-practical-property-and-contract-inventory).

Projection

: A deliberate representation derived from an authoritative model, such as a
  schema, serializer output, interface description, or documentation page.
  See [schema architectures](06-documents-schemas-dsls.qmd#four-schema-and-model-architectures).

Reference owner

: An object with shared identity or a live lifecycle whose aliases must
  observe the same evolving state. See
  [the lifecycle policies](02-values-and-state.qmd#three-lifecycle-policies).

Semantic class

: A nominal class that preserves a domain concept independently so it can
  travel through the program or participate in dispatch. See
  [the semantic carriers](03-types-and-meaning.qmd#three-carriers-of-semantics-in-s7).

Snapshot

: A value representing a fact at a point in time, often with a public policy
  that forbids revision. See
  [the lifecycle policies](02-values-and-state.qmd#three-lifecycle-policies).

Sum type

: A representation of alternatives in which a value is exactly one of several
  meaningful variants. See
  [alternatives and variants](05-composition-and-dispatch.qmd#alternatives-belong-in-the-representation).

Wire representation

: The serialized form exchanged with another system, distinct from the
  program's semantic domain model. See
  [documents and schemas](06-documents-schemas-dsls.qmd#a-document-model-is-a-contract-between-representations).
